title: Consolidate continuous batch scheduler and KV eviction paths
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and lock contention by unifying the continuous batching scheduler and the KV cache eviction paths into a single, testable control loop. Background: we currently have two overlapping mechanisms: the per-worker continuous batching loop (legacy goroutine-per-shard) and a separate eviction timer that touches the same KV cache data structures. These interact poorly under bursty traffic and large context lengths, causing mutex contention and periodic GC spikes. Work includes: 1) extract a single scheduler interface that handles batch formation, timer-driven flushes, and eviction signals; 2) centralize KV cache eviction policy (LRU + weighted size) behind that interface; 3) add async prefetch hooks for hot-prefixes; 4) remove deprecated locks and replace with shard-based atomics where safe; 5) bump runtime dependencies (tokio 1.15 -> 1.20 and jemalloc 5.3 -> 5.4) to leverage improved concurrency heaps and timers; 6) comprehensive unit + integration tests and targeted microbenchmarks. Acceptance criteria: - 95th percentile token latency reduced by >=10% on internal chat workload (seq len 1024) - CPU sys time under sustained 1k rps reduced by >=15% - No increase in memory tail events >5% across 24h test - All new public-facing API behaviors unchanged (compatibility tests green). Links: PR drafts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892, design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Batch-KV+Scheduler+Consolidation, benchmark dashboard: https://dashboards.internal.redwood.com/d/runtime/batching-kv-comp
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting notes posted; agreed to keep migration incremental and feature-flagged. Action: Miguel to prototype unified scheduler API (spike = 2 pts).

2026-02-27: Spike results: prototype reduced mutex hold time by ~40% under synthetic load (see /tmp/spike-logs). Decided to pursue central eviction policy rather than per-shard LRU to simplify correctness proofs.

2026-03-03: Rebased prototype onto latest runtime main; noticed a race when concurrent eviction and flush ran — added a lightweight epoch counter to guard iterations. Filing follow-up test ENG-4739 for deeper fuzzing.

2026-03-06: Draft PR created: runtime#1892. Requesting review from @xin-zhou and @marie. Key trade-off: using lock-free ring for batch queue vs a lock-protected VecDeque — chose ring after microbench shows 8% lower latency at 99th percentile.

2026-03-10: Benchmarks on staging (m5.4xlarge equiv): baseline 95p=134ms -> post-refactor 95p=116ms (~13.4% improvement). CPU sys decreased 18%. Memory steady with small increase in resident size (+3%). Logged results to benchmark dashboard.

2026-03-12: Security review: no sensitive surface changes; KMS paths unaffected. QA checklist started for canary rollout. Next: coordinate dedic capacity team for canary on runtime-2.04 release window.
Follow-ups: - ENG-4755: Add long-tail tracer to capture eviction-induced spikes - ENG-4761: Evaluate jemalloc tuning knobs in production - ENG-4770: Rollback plan and canary gating
